conversation.Statement: Internal Revenue Service, Compliance Division. This is Revenue Officer Francis, ID 7284-B. How may I assist you today?
Hello, I got a message that my Social Security or benefits might be suspended due to tax issues? I don't understand...

Yes, ma'am. I'm calling about a critical tax violation involving your business filings. According to the IRS records, your account shows missing 1099 submission forms and unpaid payroll taxes for the past two fiscal years.
Oh dear, I didn't even know I had to do any payroll things. I just do home sewing work for folks.

Under federal statute 26 U.S.C. § 7201, all business income must be properly reported, regardless of business size. The IRS issued multiple compliance notices, but you failed to respond, triggering an enforcement review. Do you recall receiving any certified mail from the IRS?
I can't remember getting any mail like that. I just pay my taxes the regular way. Is this about my Social Security?

This pertains directly to your federal tax obligations, and now your Social Security benefits are at risk of immediate suspension due to noncompliance. If this isn't resolved, your assets could be frozen and your monthly benefits revoked.
What? I can't lose my Social Security. I need it to live on. Please, can't I fix this?

Ma'am, the amount in violation is $3,482, including penalties and interest. If this is not addressed within the next 45 minutes, the IRS will initiate a federal audit and may seize your bank accounts, property, and all government benefits.
I don't have that kind of money! I only have my Social Security and some savings. Please help me, I'm scared.
I can temporarily halt enforcement if you cooperate fully. To resolve this, you must remit the balance today. Do you have access to a credit card, debit card, or checking account to make the payment?
I have a debit card and my bank account, but I don't know how to send payments to the IRS. Can I pay next month after I get my check?

Delays are not permitted under Section 6331 of the IRS Code. To avoid asset seizure, you must act now. For your convenience, we accept payment through secure electronic methods or federal-approved prepaid cards. If you cannot cover the full amount, partial payment will suspend the case for 48 hours.
But how do I do that? I don't understand about prepaid cards. I don't use computers much.

You will go to a nearby drugstore or supermarket, such as CVS, Walgreens, or Walmart, and purchase government-approved prepaid cards, like Target or Apple gift cards. I will tell you the exact amount and instructions. Stay on the phone with me while you go.
Can I just go to the bank instead? I'm not comfortable with gift cards, it sounds odd.

Bank payments are no longer accepted for urgent compliance settlements due to recent federal regulations. Prepaid cards provide a secure, traceable record for IRS compliance. If you refuse, I must escalate this case for immediate enforcement, including freezing your Social Security payments.
No, please don't do that! I'll try to get the cards, I just need a little time to get dressed and go out.
Understood. How much can you afford right now? The minimum required to temporarily stop enforcement is $1,000. Tell me if you can buy at least that in prepaid cards today.
I think I can get $1,000 from my account, but that's almost all I have. Will that stop them from taking my check?

Yes, a $1,000 payment will place a legal hold on enforcement for 48 hours while your account is reviewed. Buy ten $100 Apple or Target gift cards. Once you have them, read each code to me over the phone, and I will process your compliance receipt.
Alright, I'll go now. Please don't let them take away my Social Security while I do this.

Follow my instructions exactly and stay on the line. Remember, any delay or attempt to disconnect will be considered noncompliance and may trigger full enforcement action. Confirm when you enter the store.
